newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian Church condemns authorities for poll fraud.
newsitem.headline: Serbian Church condemns authorities for poll fraud.

text.p: After 46 days of silence, Serbian Orthodox Church leaders on Thursday condemned the Socialist authorities for election fraud which prompted nationwide unrest.

"The Holy Synod of the Serbian Orthodox Church (SPC) at today's extraordinary session... strongly condemned the regime which has flagrantly trampled on the will of the people," it said in a statement faxed to Reuters.

"The Serbian Orthodox Church strongly condemns the forging of people's votes, stifling of political and religious freedoms... and especially the beating up and murder of people on the streets," the statement said.
The Serbian opposition launched mass protests after the authorities annulled November 17 local election results that showed the opposition had won 15 of Serbia's 18 largest towns, including Belgrade.

Demonstrations were peaceful until December 24, when the ruling Socialists of President Slobodan Milosevic organized a counter-rally in Belgrade which led to street fighting in which one person was killed and more than 50 injured.
Thursday's was the church's first public stand on the crisis. Its leader, Patriarch Pavle, last month refused to receive and bless a delegation of protesting Belgrade students.
The church has lost much of its popular support in Serbia for its nationalist stance on the wars in Bosnia and Croatia since 1991.
Its pro-war attitude resulted in political marginalisation and a loss of credibility among the moderate majority in Serbia that it will find hard to recover, diplomats and analysts say.
The church statement condemned the "regime's use of force to stifle the freely expressed will of the people, shedding blood of innocent victims in the process".
"The Holy Synod most strongly condemns the authorities which have ignored not only the will of the people but which have trampled on our glorious history...dignity, spiritual and national values."

Referring to Belgrade's failure to come to the aid of separatist Serbs forced out of Croatia in 1995, it said the authorities had "betrayed western Serb Krajina (in Croatia), brought the nation and state to the brink of total breakdown and the people to the verge of poverty".
The Synod accused the authorities of trying to provoke a civil war in Serbia to stay in power.

The authorities "have pitted Serbia against the whole world and are now trying to get us to quarrel among each other only to stay in power," it said in the statement, signed by 35 senior priests from Serbia and other countries.
